newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND BATTLE BACK IN FIFTH TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND BATTLE BACK IN FIFTH TEST.

text.p: Batting for little more than pride with the Ashes all but lost, England skipper Michael Atherton and Alec Stewart put together an unbeaten opening stand of 76 by tea on the second day of the fifth test on Friday.
Australia, needing only a draw to retain the Ahes, had almost certainly already done enough to secure it by reaching 427 all out in their first innings.
That total represented something of a fightback by England after the touring team began the day on 302 for three.
England's bowlers persevered well in warm, humid conditions that offered some movement.
Australia's remaining seven wickets went down for 125, with the innings wrapped up shortly after lunch.

Dean Headley was the most successful England bowler, claiming four wickets for the third time in his three test matches to date. He snared Ricky Ponting (nine), Paul Reiffel (26) and Glenn McGrath (one), after claiming Matthew Elliott on Thursday, to finish with four for 87.
The Waugh brothers, who had begun the day together, did not last too long as Mark fell lbw to Andy Caddick for 68 and Steve was bowled by Devon Malcolm for 75.
Malcolm, returning to the side in place of the injured Darren Gough, also snapped up Ian Healy (16) and Shane Warne for a duck.
Wicketkeeper Stewart, straight back into the fray in England's re-jigged batting order, relished the task, dashing to a half century in 61 balls, hitting 10 fours.
Stewart was particularly harsh on Jason Gillespie, whose four overs cost 32. Atherton was more circumspect and at the interval had 18 to Stewart's 52.
